Main.sentence: William Jefferson Clinton (born William Jefferson Blythe III , August 19, 1946) is an American politician and lawyer who was the 42nd ___E:president of the United States U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_United_States)___ from 1993 to 2001. A member of the ___E:Democratic Party U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Party_(United_States))___ , he previously served as the ___E:attorney general of Arkansas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attorney_general_of_Arkansas)___ from 1977 to 1979 and as the ___E:governor of Arkansas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor_of_Arkansas)___ from 1979 to 1981, and again from 1983 to 1992. His centrist " ___E:Third Way U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Third_Way)___ " ___E:political philosophy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Democrats_(United_States))___ became known as ___E:Clintonism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clintonism)___ , which dominated ___E:his presidency U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_Bill_Clinton)___ and the succeeding decades of ___E:Democratic Party history U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_the_Democratic_Party_(United_States))___ .

Born and raised in ___E:Arkansas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arkansas)___ , Clinton graduated from ___E:Georgetown University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgetown_University)___ in 1968, and later from ___E:Yale Law School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yale_Law_School)___ , where he met his future wife, ___E:Hillary Rodham U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hillary_Clinton)___ .

After graduating from law school, Clinton returned to ___E:Arkansas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arkansas)___ and won election as state attorney general, followed by ___E:two non-consecutive tenures as Arkansas governor U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governorships_of_Bill_Clinton)___ .

As governor, he overhauled the state's education system and served as ___E:chairman U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chair_(officer))___ of the ___E:National Governors Association U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Governors_Association)___ .

Clinton was elected president in the ___E:1992 election U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_United_States_presidential_election)___ , defeating the incumbent ___E:Republican U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States))___ president ___E:George H. W. Bush U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_H._W._Bush)___ , and the independent businessman ___E:Ross Perot U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ross_Perot)___ .

He became the first president to be born in the ___E:Baby Boomer U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baby_Boomer)___ generation and the ___E:youngest U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_presidents_of_the_United_States_by_age)___ to serve two full terms.
Clinton presided over the second longest period of peacetime economic expansion in ___E:American history U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_history)___ .

He signed into law the ___E:North American Free Trade Agreement U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_American_Free_Trade_Agreement)___ and the ___E:Violent Crime Control and Law Enforcement Act U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Violent_Crime_Control_and_Law_Enforcement_Act)___ but failed to pass his plan for ___E:national health care reform U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clinton_health_care_plan_of_1993)___ .

Starting in the mid-1990s, he began an ideological evolution as he became much more conservative in his domestic policy, advocating for and signing the ___E:Personal Responsibility and Work Opportunity Act U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Personal_Responsibility_and_Work_Opportunity_Act)___ , the ___E:State Children's Health Insurance Program U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_Children%27s_Health_Insurance_Program)___ and financial deregulation measures.

He appointed ___E:Ruth Bader Ginsburg U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruth_Bader_Ginsburg)___ and ___E:Stephen Breyer U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Breyer)___ to the ___E:U.S. Supreme Court U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Supreme_Court)___ .

In foreign policy, Clinton ordered U.S. military intervention in the ___E:Bosnian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bosnian_War)___ and ___E:Kosovo wars U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kosovo_war)___ , eventually signing the ___E:Dayton Peace agreement U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dayton_Agreement)___ .

He also called for the ___E:expansion of NATO U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Expansion_of_NATO)___ in Eastern Europe and many former ___E:Warsaw Pact U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warsaw_Pact)___ members joined NATO during his presidency.

Clinton's foreign policy in the Middle East saw him sign the ___E:Iraq Liberation Act U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iraq_Liberation_Act)___ which gave aid to groups against ___E:Saddam Hussein U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saddam_Hussein)___ .

He also participated in the ___E:Oslo I Accord U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oslo_I_Accord)___ and ___E:Camp David Summit U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Camp_David_Summit)___ to advance the ___E:Israeli–Palestinian peace process U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli%E2%80%93Palestinian_peace_process)___ , and assisted the ___E:Northern Ireland peace process U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_Ireland_peace_process)___ .

Clinton won re-election in the ___E:1996 election U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1996_United_States_presidential_election)___ , defeating Republican nominee ___E:Bob Dole U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Dole)___ and returning ___E:Reform Party U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reform_Party_of_the_United_States_of_America)___ nominee Ross Perot.
In his second term, Clinton made use of ___E:permanent normal trade U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Permanent_normal_trade_relations)___ .

Many of his second term accomplishments were overshadowed by ___E:his highly publicised affair U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clinton%E2%80%93Lewinsky_scandal)___ with ___E:White House U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_House)___ intern ___E:Monica Lewinsky U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monica_Lewinsky)___ , when it was revealed in early 1998 that the two had been engaging in an eighteen-month-long sexual relationship.

This scandal escalated throughout the year, culminating in December when ___E:Clinton was impeached U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Impeachment_of_Bill_Clinton)___ by the ___E:House of Representatives U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_of_Representatives)___ , becoming the first U.S. president to be impeached since ___E:Andrew Johnson U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Johnson)___ .

The two impeachment articles that the House passed were centered around ___E:perjury U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perjury)___ and Clinton using the powers of the presidency to commit obstruction of justice.

In January 1999, ___E:Clinton's impeachment trial U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Impeachment_trial_of_Bill_Clinton)___ began in the ___E:Senate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate)___ , where he was acquitted two months later on both charges.

During the last three years of Clinton's presidency, the ___E:Congressional Budget Office U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congressional_Budget_Office)___ reported a budget surplus—the first and only such surplus since 1969.
Clinton left office in 2001 with the joint-highest approval rating of any U.S. president.
His presidency ranks among the middle to upper tier in ___E:historical rankings of U.S. presidents U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Historical_rankings_of_U.S._presidents)___ .
His personal conduct and ___E:misconduct allegations U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Clinton_sexual_assault_and_misconduct_allegations)___ have made him the subject of substantial scrutiny.

Since leaving office, Clinton has been involved in public speaking and humanitarian work. He created the ___E:Clinton Foundation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clinton_Foundation)___ to address international causes such as the prevention of HIV/AIDS and global warming.
In 2009, he was named the ___E:United Nations special envoy to Haiti U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special_Envoy_of_the_Secretary-General)___ .

After the ___E:2010 Haiti earthquake U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_Haiti_earthquake)___ , Clinton founded the ___E:Clinton Bush Haiti Fund U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clinton_Bush_Haiti_Fund)___ with ___E:George W. Bush U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush)___ .

He has remained active in Democratic Party politics, campaigning for his wife's ___E:2008 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hillary_Clinton_2008_presidential_campaign)___ and ___E:2016 presidential campaigns U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hillary_Clinton_2016_presidential_campaign)___ .

Following ___E:Jimmy Carter U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Carter)___ 's ___E:death U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Death_and_state_funeral_of_Jimmy_Carter)___ in December 2024, he is the earliest-serving living former U.S. president and the last surviving president to have served in the 20th century.
Clinton was born William Jefferson Blythe III on August 19, 1946, at Julia Chester Hospital in ___E:Hope, Arkansas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hope,_Arkansas)___ .

He is the son of ___E:William Jefferson Blythe Jr. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Jefferson_Blythe_Jr.)___ , a traveling salesman who died in an automobile accident three months before his birth, and ___E:Virginia Dell Cassidy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virginia_Clinton_Kelley)___ (later Virginia Kelley).

His parents married on September 4, 1943, but this union later proved bigamous, as Blythe was still married to his fourth wife.  Virginia traveled to ___E:New Orleans U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Orleans)___ to study nursing soon after Bill was born, leaving him in Hope with her parents Eldridge and Edith Cassidy, who owned and ran a small grocery store.

At a time when the southern United States was ___E:racially segregated U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Racial_segregation_in_the_United_States)___ , Clinton's grandparents sold goods on ___E:credit U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Credit_(finance))___ to people of all races.

In 1950, Bill's mother returned from nursing school and married ___E:Roger Clinton Sr. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Clinton_Sr.)___ , who co-owned an ___E:automobile dealership U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Car_dealership)___ in ___E:Hot Springs, Arkansas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hot_Springs,_Arkansas)___ , with his brother and ___E:Earl T. Ricks U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earl_T._Ricks)___ .

The family moved to Hot Springs in 1950.  Although he immediately assumed use of his stepfather's surname, it was not until Clinton turned 15  that he formally adopted the surname Clinton as a gesture toward him.  Clinton has described his stepfather as a gambler and an alcoholic who regularly abused his family.
The physical abuse only ceased after a then-14-year-old Bill challenged his stepfather to "stand and face" him, though the verbal abuse continued.
Bill would eventually forgive Roger Sr. for his abusive actions near the latter's death.

In Hot Springs, Clinton attended St. John's Catholic Elementary School, Ramble Elementary School, and the ___E:segregated U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/School_segregation_in_the_United_States)___ ___E:Hot Springs High School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hot_Springs_High_School_(Arkansas))___ , where he was an active student leader, avid reader, and musician.
Clinton was in the chorus and played the ___E:tenor saxophone U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenor_saxophone)___ , winning first chair in the state band's saxophone section.

While in high school, Clinton performed for two years in a jazz trio, The 3 Kings, with ___E:Randy Goodrum U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Randy_Goodrum)___ , who became a successful professional pianist.

In 1961, Clinton became a member of the Hot Springs Chapter of the ___E:Order of DeMolay U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeMolay_International)___ , a youth group affiliated with ___E:Freemasonry U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freemasonry)___ , but he never became a Freemason.
He briefly considered dedicating his life to music, but felt that his musical skills would never match the skills of the best musicians, so pursued politics instead.

Clinton began an interest in law at Hot Springs High when he took up the challenge to argue the defense of the ancient ___E:Roman senator U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_Senator)___ ___E:Catiline U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catiline)___ in a mock trial in his Latin class.
After a vigorous defense that made use of his "budding rhetorical and political skills", he told the Latin teacher Elizabeth Buck it "made him realize that someday he would study law".
Clinton has identified two influential moments in his life, both occurring in 1963, that contributed to his decision to become a public figure.

One was his visit as a ___E:Boys Nation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boys_Nation)___ senator to the ___E:White House U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_House)___ to meet President ___E:John F. Kennedy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy)___ .

The other was watching ___E:Martin Luther King Jr. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_Luther_King_Jr.)___ 's 1963 " ___E:I Have a Dream U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Have_a_Dream)___ " speech on TV, which impressed him so much that he later memorized it.

With the aid of scholarships, Clinton attended the ___E:School of Foreign Service U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/School_of_Foreign_Service)___ at ___E:Georgetown University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgetown_University)___ in Washington, D.C., receiving a ___E:Bachelor of Science U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor_of_Science)___ in foreign service in 1968. Georgetown was the only university where Clinton applied.
In 1964 and 1965, Clinton won elections for ___E:class president U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Class_president)___ .
From 1964 to 1967, he was an intern and then a clerk in the office of Arkansas senator ___E:J. William Fulbright U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J._William_Fulbright)___ .

While in college, he became a brother of service fraternity ___E:Alpha Phi Omega U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alpha_Phi_Omega)___  and was elected to ___E:Phi Beta Kappa U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phi_Beta_Kappa)___ .
He is a member of ___E:Kappa Kappa Psi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kappa_Kappa_Psi)___ honorary band fraternity.

Upon graduating from Georgetown in 1968, Clinton won a ___E:Rhodes Scholarship U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodes_Scholarship)___ to ___E:University College, Oxford U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_College,_Oxford)___ , where he initially read for a ___E:B.Phil. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B.Phil.)___ in ___E:philosophy, politics, and economics U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philosophy,_Politics,_and_Economics)___ but transferred to a ___E:B.Litt. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor_of_Letters)___ in politics and, ultimately, a B.Phil. in politics.
Clinton did not expect to return for the second year because of the draft and so he switched programs; this type of activity was common among other Rhodes Scholars from his cohort.
He was offered to study at ___E:Yale Law School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yale_Law_School)___ , so he left early to return to the United States and did not receive a degree from Oxford.
Clinton befriended fellow American Rhodes Scholar Frank Aller during his time at Oxford.

In 1969, Aller received a ___E:draft U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Draft_lottery_(1969))___ letter that mandated deployment to the ___E:Vietnam War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vietnam_War)___ .
Aller's 1971 suicide had an influential impact on Clinton.

British writer and feminist ___E:Sara Maitland U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sara_Maitland)___ said of Clinton, "I remember Bill and Frank Aller taking me to a pub in Walton Street in the summer term of 1969 and talking to me about the Vietnam War. I knew nothing about it, and when Frank began to describe the napalming of civilians I began to cry. Bill said that feeling bad wasn't good enough.
That was the first time I encountered the idea that liberal sensitivities weren't enough and you had to do something about such things".

Clinton was a member of the ___E:Oxford University Basketball Club U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oxford_University_Men%27s_Basketball)___ and also played for Oxford University's ___E:rugby union U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rugby_union)___ team.

While Clinton was president in 1994, he received an honorary ___E:Doctor of Civil Law U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_of_Civil_Law)___ degree and a fellowship from the ___E:University of Oxford U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Oxford)___ , specifically for being "a doughty and tireless champion of the cause of world peace", having "a powerful collaborator in his wife", and for winning "general applause for his achievement of resolving the gridlock that prevented an agreed budget".

During the Vietnam War, Clinton received educational draft deferments while he was in England in 1968 and 1969.  While at Oxford, he participated in ___E:Vietnam War protests U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Opposition_to_the_Vietnam_War)___ and organized a ___E:Moratorium to End the War in Vietnam U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moratorium_to_End_the_War_in_Vietnam)___ event in October 1969.  He was planning to attend law school in the U.S. and knew he might lose his deferment.

Clinton tried unsuccessfully to obtain positions in the ___E:National Guard U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Guard_of_the_United_States)___ and the ___E:Air Force officer candidate school U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_Force_Officer_Training_School)___ , and he then made arrangements to join the ___E:Reserve Officers' Training Corps U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reserve_Officers%27_Training_Corps)___ (ROTC) program at the ___E:University of Arkansas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Arkansas)___ .

He subsequently decided not to join the ROTC, saying in a letter to the officer in charge of the program that he opposed the war, but did not think it was honorable to use ROTC, National Guard, or Reserve service to avoid serving in Vietnam.

He further stated that because he opposed the war, he would not volunteer to serve in uniform, but would subject himself to the draft, and would serve if selected only as a way "to maintain my political viability within the system".

Clinton registered for the draft and received a high number (311), meaning that those whose birthdays had been drawn as numbers 1 to 310 would be ___E:drafted U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Draft_lottery_(1969))___ before him, making it unlikely he would be called up. (In fact, the highest number drafted was 195.)  ___E:Colonel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colonel_(United_States))___ Eugene Holmes, the Army officer involved with Clinton's ROTC application, issued a ___E:notarized U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Notarize)___ statement during the 1992 presidential campaign stating that he suspected Clinton attempted to manipulate the situation to avoid the draft.

During the 1992 campaign, it was revealed that Clinton's uncle had attempted to secure him a position in the ___E:Navy Reserve U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Navy_Reserve)___ , which would have prevented him from being deployed to Vietnam.

This effort was unsuccessful and Clinton said in 1992 that he had been unaware of it until then.  Although legal, Clinton's actions with respect to the draft and deciding whether to serve in the military were criticized during his first presidential campaign by conservatives and some Vietnam veterans, some of whom charged that he had used Fulbright's influence to avoid military service.

Clinton's 1992 campaign manager, ___E:James Carville U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Carville)___ , successfully argued that Clinton's letter in which he declined to join the ROTC should be made public, insisting that voters, many of whom had also opposed the Vietnam War, would understand and appreciate his position.

After Oxford, Clinton attended Yale Law School and earned a ___E:Juris Doctor U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juris_Doctor)___ (J.D.) degree in 1973.  In 1971, he met his future wife, Hillary Rodham, in the ___E:Yale Law Library U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lillian_Goldman_Law_Library)___ ; she was a class year ahead of him.  They began dating and were soon inseparable.

After only about a month, Clinton postponed his summer plans to be a coordinator for the ___E:George McGovern U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_McGovern)___ ___E:campaign U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_McGovern_presidential_campaign,_1972)___ for the ___E:1972 United States presidential election U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1972_United_States_presidential_election)___ to move in with her in California.
The couple continued ___E:living together U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohabitating)___ in New Haven when they returned to law school.

Clinton eventually ___E:moved to Texas with Rodham in 1972 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1972_United_States_presidential_election_in_Texas#McGovern_campaign)___ to take a job leading McGovern's effort there.
He spent considerable time in ___E:Dallas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas)___ , at the campaign's local headquarters on Lemmon Avenue, where he had an office.

Clinton worked with future two-term ___E:mayor of Dallas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_mayors_of_Dallas)___ ___E:Ron Kirk U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ron_Kirk)___ ,  future ___E:governor of Texas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_governors_of_Texas)___ ___E:Ann Richards U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ann_Richards)___ ,  and then unknown television director and filmmaker ___E:Steven Spielberg U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Spielberg)___ .

After graduating from ___E:Yale Law School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yale_Law_School)___ , Clinton returned to Arkansas and became a law professor at the ___E:University of Arkansas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Arkansas)___ .
In 1974, he ran for the ___E:House of Representatives U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_of_Representatives)___ .

Running in the conservative ___E:3rd district U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arkansas%27s_3rd_congressional_district)___ against incumbent Republican ___E:John Paul Hammerschmidt U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Paul_Hammerschmidt)___ , Clinton's campaign was bolstered by the anti-Republican and anti-incumbent mood resulting from the ___E:Watergate scandal U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Watergate_scandal)___ .
Hammerschmidt, who had received 77 percent of the vote in 1972, defeated Clinton by only a 52 percent to 48 percent margin.
In 1976, Clinton ran for ___E:Arkansas attorney general U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arkansas_Attorney_General)___ .
Defeating the secretary of state and the deputy attorney general in the Democratic primary, Clinton was elected with no opposition in the general election, as no Republican had run for the office.
In 1978, Clinton entered the Arkansas gubernatorial primary.
At just 31 years old, he was one of the youngest gubernatorial candidates in the state's history.

Clinton was elected ___E:Governor of Arkansas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor_of_Arkansas)___ in ___E:1978 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1978_Arkansas_gubernatorial_election)___ , having defeated the Republican candidate ___E:Lynn Lowe U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lynn_Lowe)___ , a farmer from ___E:Texarkana U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texarkana,_Arkansas)___ .
Clinton was only 32 years old when he took office, the youngest governor in the country at the time and the second youngest governor in the history of Arkansas.
Due to his youthful appearance, Clinton was often called the "Boy Governor".
He worked on educational reform and directed the maintenance of Arkansas's roads, with wife Hillary leading a successful committee on urban health care reform.

However, his term included an unpopular motor vehicle tax and citizens' anger over the escape of Cuban refugees (from the ___E:Mariel boatlift U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mariel_boatlift)___ ) detained in ___E:Fort Chaffee U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Chaffee)___ in 1980. Monroe Schwarzlose, of ___E:Kingsland U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingsland,_Arkansas)___ in ___E:Cleveland County U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cleveland_County,_Arkansas)___ , polled 31 percent of the vote against Clinton in the Democratic gubernatorial primary of 1980. Some suggested Schwarzlose's unexpected voter turnout foreshadowed Clinton's defeat by Republican challenger ___E:Frank D. White U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_D._White)___ in the general election that year. As Clinton once joked, he was the youngest ex-governor in the nation's history.
After leaving office in January 1981, Clinton joined friend ___E:Bruce Lindsey U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruce_Lindsey)___ 's Little Rock law firm of Wright, Lindsey and Jennings.
In 1982, he was elected governor a second time and kept the office for ten years.
Effective with the 1986 election, Arkansas had changed its gubernatorial term of office from two to four years.
During his term, he helped transform Arkansas's economy and improved the state's educational system.

For ___E:senior citizens U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Senior_citizen)___ , he removed the ___E:sales tax U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sales_tax)___ from medications and increased the home property-tax exemption.

He became a leading figure among the ___E:New Democrats U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Democrats_(United_States))___ , a group of ___E:Democrats U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Party_(United_States))___ who advocated welfare reform, smaller government, and other policies not supported by liberals.

Formally organized as the ___E:Democratic Leadership Council U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Leadership_Council)___ (DLC), the New Democrats argued that in light of President ___E:Ronald Reagan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronald_Reagan)___ 's ___E:landslide victory in 1984 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1984_United_States_presidential_election)___ , the Democratic Party needed to adopt a more centrist political stance in order to succeed at the national level.

Clinton delivered the ___E:Democratic response U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_response_to_the_State_of_the_Union_address)___ to Reagan's ___E:1985 State of the Union Address U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1985_State_of_the_Union_Address)___ and served as chair of the ___E:National Governors Association U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Governors_Association)___ from 1986 to 1987, bringing him to an audience beyond Arkansas.
In the early 1980s, Clinton made reform of the Arkansas education system a top priority of his gubernatorial administration.

The Arkansas Education Standards Committee was chaired by Clinton's wife Hillary, who was also an attorney as well as the chair of the ___E:Legal Services Corporation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legal_Services_Corporation)___ .
The committee transformed Arkansas's education system.

Proposed reforms included more spending for schools (supported by a sales-tax increase), better opportunities for gifted children, vocational education, higher teachers' salaries, more course variety, and compulsory teacher competency exams.
The reforms passed in September 1983 after Clinton called a special ___E:legislative session U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arkansas_General_Assembly)___ —the longest in Arkansas history.
Many have considered this the greatest achievement of the Clinton governorship.

He defeated four Republican candidates for governor: Lowe (1978), White (1982 and 1986), ___E:Jonesboro U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jonesboro,_Arkansas)___ businessmen ___E:Woody Freeman U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woody_Freeman)___ (1984), and ___E:Sheffield Nelson U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sheffield_Nelson)___ of Little Rock (1990).

Also in the 1980s, the Clintons' personal and business affairs included transactions that became the basis of the ___E:Whitewater controversy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whitewater_controversy)___ investigation, which later dogged his presidential administration.
After extensive investigation over several years, no indictments were made against the Clintons related to the years in Arkansas.

According to some sources, Clinton was a ___E:death penalty U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capital_punishment_in_the_United_States)___ opponent in his early years, but he eventually switched positions.
